what_it_does: The paper argues that the data center's performance bottleneck has shifted from raw computation to memory—specifically, how fast data can be read from and written to memory, and how far away that memory sits. Modern CPUs and GPUs are so fast at math that they spend most of their time waiting for data, not doing math. The work proposes changes to how memory is organized, how much bandwidth connects the memory to the compute chips, and how different memory levels work together. This is a fundamental rethinking of data center architecture around memory instead of compute.
